correctness.rationale: Full proof reconstructed: a rose blank-return loop rotates exactly the nonhub tokens on its petal, yielding a free direct product of cyclic label rotations; each nonhub state has a unique recovery path to a hub state; the exact edge subdivision includes the C2 parallel-edge exception. For spanning trees, every subdivided path outside a base tree omits exactly one segment, giving the weighted-tree formula; Fourier eigenvalues of each cyclic multigraph are 4sin^2(pi*k/d), with weighted matrix-tree normalization 1/L. Exact independent enumeration and integer determinants agree for five nontrivial parameter tuples. The all-triangle closed product follows from binomial multiplicities; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The exact connected-component graph structure, cyclomatic ranks and an all-parameter spanning-tree count for an infinite family with arbitrarily many and unequal petals is a natural classification of sliding-puzzle configuration graphs. Spanning trees quantify connecting reconfiguration backbones and are not supplied by connectivity alone. The explicit uniform-triangle specialization is meaningful for the well-known friendship-graph rose family. This is neither a one-off parameter calculation nor a routine rewriting of known component-size data.
